A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DuET research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original object-detection experiments, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and computational measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds Night Rainy evaluation results and training-time measurements in Table S14.

M1.justification: The parameter decomposition, layer-wise merging rule, incremental head, distillation loss, and Directional Consistency Loss remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 and the methodological equations retain the same procedures; the new background-shift discussion explains the existing method.

E1.justification: Table S14 adds Daytime Sunny [1:4] → Night Rainy [5:7], extending weather coverage to nighttime rain. This increases the reported experiments from six to seven while retaining the existing Pascal and weather scenarios.

E2.justification: All corresponding existing experiments retain their comparison methods. Table S14 uses established baseline families—LDB, CL-DETR, LwF, and ERD. Its additional CL-DETR/RT-DETR-l configuration changes the backbone setting without documenting a new comparison algorithm.

E3.justification: The added experiment evaluates CL-DETR with RT-DETR-l, whereas v1 reports CL-DETR with Deformable DETR. Table S14 also introduces total T1+T2 training-time measurement on one NVIDIA A100-PCIE-40GB. Existing training budgets, batch sizes, task splits, and accuracy metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 extends computational analysis to comparative training cost through Table S14; v1 reported FLOPs, parameters, inference speed, and memory. Component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity, class/domain-order analyses, and qualitative case studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same ± reporting and the same permutation standard deviations in Table S4. The added result rows follow the existing practice, without new seed counts, repeated-run disclosures, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Table S14 adds performance and timing results: DuET/YOLO11n achieves RAI 60.92 versus ERD's 45.39, but lower Avg GI, 34.18 versus 38.96. Existing tables and plots retain their numerical results. Section 5.2 newly states car mAP increasing from 49.4 to 71.8 without a matching class-level table. Appendix E.1 adds aggregate summaries, but its claimed +11.98% RAI gain over LDB does not match the tabulated mean differences: approximately 9.53 points over the original six experiments or 8.37 including Night Rainy.

T1.justification: The formal task assumptions, task-vector and loss equations, and RI/GI/RAI definitions remain unchanged, including Appendix A's metric derivations and Appendix B's loss formulation. No theorem, proof, or new mathematical argument is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about exemplar-free dual incremental detection, detector-agnostic task arithmetic, Directional Consistency Loss, and RAI. The headline performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: New Appendix F explicitly attributes background-shift mitigation to preserving previous object representations through parameter decomposition and merging. Appendix E.1 adds the interpretation that matched-backbone gains are method-specific rather than backbone-dependent. The limitations concerning pretrained weights and linear merging are retained, moving from Appendix G to H.

D1.justification: Appendix C.4 and Table S14 newly disclose the single A100-PCIE-40GB hardware setting and per-method training hours. Appendix D's implementation settings and software link remain unchanged. Night Rainy sample counts are not added to the dataset-statistics table.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhong, Jiao and Bao's 2025 work on replay-based incremental object detection to the discussion of exemplar-dependent methods. Research positioning otherwise remains stable. Removing the duplicated Augmented Box Replay reference is bibliographic cleanup, not removal of a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized copyediting, spelling adjustments, a corresponding-author annotation, and short explanatory additions. Inserting Background Shift as Appendix F moves Dataset Statistics and Limitations to G and H; the main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table S14 with performance and training-time columns, alongside modest spacing, emphasis, and page-flow adjustments. Existing figures use identical graphic assets, and retained tables preserve their display structures.

improvement.justification: The additional Night Rainy comparison and hardware-specific training times modestly strengthen empirical coverage and computational-cost transparency. These benefits are tempered by missing sample counts for the added setting and the new aggregate LDB-gain claim that does not reconcile with the tables. The core method and principal evidence remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
